newsitem.title: UK: Briton freed early from Indian drugs sentence.
newsitem.headline: Briton freed early from Indian drugs sentence.

text.p: A British woman has been freed from an Indian prison after serving two years of a 10-year sentence for possession of drugs following an appeal from Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, the Foreign Office said on Friday.

A Foreign Office spokesman said Samantha Slater, 25, who was convicted in July 1994 of possessing charas, or cannabis resin, had been pardoned and released on Thursday from Trissur central prison in Kerala state.
"It is very good news for Samantha and her family. We worked hard for this, and are grateful to the Indian authorities for this outcome," the spokesman said.

Successive British high commissioners had pressed for a pardon because the sentence was deemed severe in relation to the small amount of the drug involved. Rifkind had also raised the matter during his official visit to India in August.
